title: InVita D3 50,000 IU soft capsules: summary of product characteristics
authors: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Consilient Health Limited (marketing authorisation holder)
journal: MHRA Products, marketing authorisation PL 24837/0074; date of revision of the text 21 July 2016
funder: not stated; UK product information carries no funding statement.
result: Indication: treatment of vitamin D3 deficiency; for deficiency below 25 nmol/L, 50,000 IU weekly for 6 to 8 weeks, then maintenance. Contraindications: hypercalcaemia or hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis or nephrocalcinosis, serious renal impairment, hypervitaminosis D, pseudohypoparathyroidism, pregnancy, age under 18 years. Warnings: caution in renal impairment, with risk of soft tissue calcification; caution in sarcoidosis because of increased conversion to the active form; no clear evidence of causation between vitamin D3 and renal stones, but the risk is plausible, especially with calcium supplementation; a single annual oral bolus of 500,000 IU was reported to increase fractures in elderly subjects, with the greatest increase in the first 3 months after dosing. Interactions: thiazides reduce urinary calcium; vitamin D3 may increase the risk of digitalis toxicity (arrhythmia). Undesirable effects: hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria uncommon (more than 1/1000, less than 1/100). Overdose: the threshold for intoxication is 40,000 to 100,000 IU daily for 1 to 2 months in adults with normal parathyroid function; infants and small children may react to far lower amounts; overdose causes hypercalcaemic syndrome with calcium deposits in kidneys (nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis) and vessels; the often persisting and in some circumstances life-threatening hypercalcaemia takes several weeks to normalise after the preparation is stopped. Preclinical: prolonged hypercalcaemia caused calcification mainly in kidneys, heart, aorta, testes, thymus and intestinal mucosa.
